readme:
Ryugi (流儀) — Interactive Artifacts for Coding Agents

ryoo-ghee · [ɾʲɯːɡʲi] · Japanese for “a school's own way of doing things”

Interactive artboards, design docs, whiteboards, HTML benches, slides and verify reports for coding agents.
Your agent draws its options instead of describing them in Markdown. Pick, comment and send feedback straight back to your agent session.

Ask an agent for a settings page and you get three paragraphs describing three layouts. Ask for a design and you get a wall of Markdown you can't point at. Ryugi gives the agent pages to put that work on, and gives you a way to answer on them: - **Artboard** — every option drawn side by side; pick one. - **Document** — a design doc with the agent's questions inline; comment on any sentence. - **Whiteboard** — boxes and arrows you both draw on. - **HTML** — one page with real sliders to tune a component or a motion. - **Slides** — a deck the agent writes and you present, with your notes on a second screen; fix any slide by hand. - **Verify** — the built screen next to what you approved, and a report of what the agent proved by running it; pass or reject. Your picks, comments and verdicts go straight back to the agent session that made the page. Every artifact lives in your project, opens from one local server, and becomes a link when you want to share it. ```bash npx ryugi-artifacts install ```

Works with Claude Code · Codex · Cursor · Gemini CLI · OpenCode · Copilot CLI · Pi · Antigravity · Kimi Code · Qwen Code · Devin · Droid

Free and local-first: artifacts live in your project and open from a local server, no account needed. In Claude Code, a comment you pin reaches the agent on its own — it edits, replies under your comment, and the page updates while you watch. Publish to Ryugi Cloud only when you want a link. The terminal wizard installs a persistent `ryugi` command, lets you select one or more harnesses, then asks which content to install: - **Artifacts only** — send `Show me three directions for a settings page` and an artboard opens. - **The full workflow** — artifacts plus skills that brainstorm, spec, build under TDD and verify. Send `Let's make a react todo list` and the agent opens an artboard before it writes code.

Harnesses · CLI · Full workflow · Ryugi Cloud

## Artboard — choose instead of imagine **Use it when** there is more than one way it could look. The agent draws every option side by side and marks the one it recommends. Pick, comment on any pixel, and Submit sends your answer back. ## Document — design docs you can argue with **Use it when** the decision is structure, architecture or tradeoffs. The agent asks its questions inside the doc and links the boards it drew. Comment on a sentence or edit in place; your edits and the agent's merge live. ## Whiteboard — sketch the structure together **Use it when** the parts and arrows are still the question. You both draw on it. Select what you drew, ask about it, and the answer lands next to your sketch. ## HTML — tune it with real controls **Use it when** one thing needs tuning: a component, a type scale, a motion. A one-page bench whose sliders keep their values when the agent rewrites the page. ## Slides — a deck you can present **Use it when** you will stand in front of people with it: a talk, a team share-out, a launch. The agent writes the deck and it follows your light or dark look. Present it full screen, or in presenter mode with your notes and the next slide on your screen and the audience on another. Click a slide to fix a word, restyle or move a block yourself, or pin a comment for the agent. ## Verify — you pass or reject **Use it when** the work is built and you decide whether it matches. The built page sits next to the design you approved. Pass it, or reject it and say what is off; it comes back fixed. What a screen can't show goes in a **verify report**: one line per claim the agent checked by running something — a test run, an API response, a migration count, which build is deployed — with the raw output one click away, and a "Not verified" list of what it couldn't check and why. You read it top to bottom and pass, reject or waive; screens still get judged on the artboard, and the report links to them. ## Comments go back to the agent **Use it when** you'd rather point at the thing than describe it in the terminal. Pin a comment on a board, a sentence or a sketch, and it reaches the agent session that opened the page. In Claude Code it arrives on its own, with no message from you; the agent applies it, replies under your comment and updates the page while you watch. Questions, picks and verdicts travel the same way. ## Library — every artifact, one server **Use it when** you want last week's mockup back, or a link to share. ```bash npx ryugi-artifacts ``` Local first, no subscription, no agent session needed. One server covers every project on the machine, with ⌘K to jump and links that survive a restart. `publish` shares one to [Ryugi Cloud](https://ryugi.innei.dev). For a persistent `ryugi` command without a harness plugin: ```bash npx ryugi-artifacts install --mode artifacts --harness none ryugi ryugi /path/to/project ``` Node.js 20.12 or newer is required. The installer keeps a complete runtime outside the npx cache and creates `~/.local/bin/ryugi` (a command shim on Windows). It prints PATH instructions for your shell. `npm install -g ryugi-artifacts` remains available; package-manager installations keep their original update channel. `ryugi update` updates the CLI and recorded plugins; `ryugi doctor` checks the install and `ryugi uninstall` removes owned entries while retaining artifacts and user data. See the [CLI guide](docs/artifacts-cli.md) for commands and options. ## Add the full workflow Artifacts work on their own. If you also want the agent to build from what you approved, pick the full workflow at install (or run `ryugi install --mode full --harness codex,pi` later). Its skills make the agent reach for the artifacts at the right moment, and they fire on their own: ```mermaid flowchart LR I[Idea] --> B[Brainstorm] --> A[Artifacts] --> S[Spec] --> T[Build · TDD] --> V[Verify] --> L[Land] ``` After you sign off, the agent slices the spec into tasks, proves each one red-green, keeps a ledger of judgment calls across compaction, gets one fresh review of the branch, and reports how to land it. Debugging and worktrees are covered too. [How it works →](docs/workflow.md) ## Work with your harness Have Node.js and npm available in the agent's environment. The plugin calls its own launcher, which downloads `ryugi-artifacts` on first use and caches each release under `~/.cache/ryugi/artifacts/` by default. It checks for updates at most once a day and can reuse a compatible cached release offline. The first run needs network access and a writable cache. ### Claude Code settings Ryugi replaces Claude's hosted Artifacts with the Artboard, documents, whiteboards, HTML benches and decks. Turn the hosted ones off by adding this key to the top level of `~/.claude/settings.json` — keep your other settings: ```json { "disableArtifact": true } ``` That is the only flag Ryugi needs; leave the rest of your Claude Code settings alone.
Other harnesses | Harness | Command | | ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Antigravity | `agy plugin install https://github.com/Innei/ryugi` | | Codex, Cursor | Add this repo as a local plugin source ([detail](docs/install.md#codex-cursor)) | | Devin CLI | `devin plugins install Innei/ryugi` | | Factory Droid | `droid plugin marketplace add https://github.com/Innei/ryugi` then `droid plugin install ryugi@ryugi` | | Gemini CLI | `gemini extensions install https://github.com/Innei/ryugi` | | Kimi Code | `/plugins install https://github.com/Innei/ryugi` | | OpenCode | [.opencode/INSTALL.md](.opencode/INSTALL.md) | | Pi | `pi install git:github.com/Innei/ryugi` | | Qwen Code | `qwen extensions install Innei/ryugi` | | Hermes Agent | `hermes plugins install Innei/ryugi --enable` | | Muse | `muse plugins install ./` then `muse plugins approve ryugi` | | DeepSeek Harness | `dsh plugin --profile add link:/path/to/ryugi/.dsh` ([detail](docs/README.dsh.md)) | Updates and caveats: [docs/install.md](docs/install.md).
## Credits Fork of [Superpowers](https://github.com/obra/superpowers) v7.0.0 by Jesse Vincent and [Prime Radiant](https://primeradiant.com) ([UPSTREAM.md](UPSTREAM.md)). [Issues](https://github.com/Innei/ryugi/issues) and PRs welcome; [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) has the rules. ## License Skills, harness integrations and docs: [Ryugi License 1.1](LICENSE) — free to use, modify and redistribute, with two exceptions. The Restricted Parties in Schedule A (Tencent, Alibaba, ByteDance, Baidu, Huawei, Xiaomi, Meituan, JD, PDD, NetEase, Kuaishou, Didi, Ant Group, iFlytek, SenseTime, and products such as WorkBuddy, Qwen, Qoder and Trae) may use and modify the skills for their own internal work, their employees included, but may not list them in a marketplace, ship them in a product, or train models on them for others; and nobody may scrape the skills into a marketplace. This is source-available, not an open source license; material derived from Superpowers and contributions made before 2026-11-04 stay MIT (Exhibit B). The artifacts application, published to npm as [`ryugi-artifacts`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/ryugi-artifacts), is proprietary (npm `license`: `UNLICENSED`) and not part of this repository.
